title: Microfluidic Chip Fabrication and Method to Detect Influenza
protocol: Make two plaques from Zeonex 690R pellets.
Distribute 8-9 grams of Zeonex pellets evenly in the center of a metal plate.
Preheat the plate on a heated press at 198 °C for 5 minutes.
Apply pressure slowly to 2,500 psi and hold for another 5 minutes.
Emboss the microfluidic channel in the plaque with an epoxy mold.
Preheat the plaque and mold on a heated press at 157 °C for 10 minutes.
Apply pressure slowly to 1,000 psi and hold for another 10 minutes.
Remove the plaque from the mold by hand or using tongs before it cools down.
Drill holes in the embossed chip at the inlet, waste port, and outlet of the microfluidic channel.
Wash the chips with IPA, RNAse Away, and deionized water sequentially.
Air dry the chips.
Preheat the chips on a heated press at 131 °C for 10 minutes.
Press the chips together at 350 psi for another 10 minutes.
Attach Nanoports at the inlet, waste, and outlet ports separately using J-B Weld Epoxy.
Cure the attached ports for 15 to 24 hours as per manufacturer's instructions.
Rinse the SPE channel with 50 μl RNAse Away.
Follow the rinse with 100 μl nuclease free water.
Load the SPE channel with 4 μl of the grafting solution (methyl methacrylate with 3% w/v benzophenone).
Crosslink the methacrylate by incubating for 10 min in a UV oven under 365 nm UV wavelength and 2,000 mJ/cm².
Remove the residual grafting solution using vacuum.

Make the SPE column solution (all v/v %): 16% ethylene dimethacrylate, 24% butyl methacrylate, 42% 1-dodecanol, 18% cyclohexanol, and add 1% 2-dimethylamino-4-(methylphenylamino)phenol as the photo-initiator.
Take out the same volume of silica microspheres solution as the SPE column solution to make a 1:1 mixture.
Completely dry the mixture at 70 °C overnight in a vacuum oven.
Break up the pellet by tapping on the tube with the lid closed.
Add the SPE column solution into the dried silica microsphere tube and vortex to mix thoroughly.
Load 4 μl of the SPE solution into the same channel.
Crosslink it by UV irradiation for 2.5 min.
Flip the chip over and irradiate for another 2.5 min.
The polymerized SPE column should appear as an opaque white solid.
Wash the channel with 500 μl of 100% methanol to rinse away excess reactants.
Attach two thin-film heaters to the bottom of the chip with thermally conductive tape.
Place five thermocouples into the chip through the dead-ended open side channels.
Prepare 96 μl of 70% ethanol with DEPC-treated and autoclaved water.
Add 4 μl of 25X RNA Secure to 96 μl of 70% ethanol in one tube.
Duplicate the same mixture with 100% ethanol in a separate tube.
Prepare 300 μl of channel buffer by mixing 75 μl of 6 M guanidine thiocyanate, 150 μl of 2-propanol, and 63 μl of nuclease-free water.
Add 12 μl of 25X RNA Secure to the channel buffer mixture.
Prepare 312 μl of lysis buffer by mixing 100 μl of 6 M guanidine thiocyanate, 200 μl of 2-propanol, and 12 μl of 25X RNA Secure.
Heat the 70% ethanol, 100% ethanol, channel buffer, and lysis buffers at 60 °C for 10-20 min to activate the RNA Secure.
Run the channel buffer through the SPE channel at a flow rate of 0.8 ml/hr to equilibrate the microfluidic channel.
Quick-thaw the test sample in VTM at 37 °C in a water bath.
Remove the sample from the water bath immediately after it is thawed.
Centrifuge the sample at 13,000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Transfer 100 μl of the supernatant into 300 μl of lysis buffer.
Add 6 μl of 1 μg/μl carrier RNA to complete the mixture.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Spin the mixture for 5 seconds.
Load the entire lysate into a Luer-lok 1 cc syringe.
Run the lysate through the SPE channel at a flow rate of 0.8 ml/hr.
Wash the SPE channel with 100 μl of 70% ethanol at 1 ml/hr.
Wash the SPE channel with 100 μl of 100% ethanol at 1 ml/hr.
Position an empty syringe at the 0.5 ml mark and push air through the channel to dry it at 1 ml/hr.
Run 67.5 μl of nuclease-free water through the channel to elute bound nucleic acids at 0.5 ml/hr.
Collect 13.5 μl from the nanoport at the waste port during the elution step.
Prepare 36.5 μl of RT-PCR master mix using reagents from a Qiagen OneStep RT-PCR kit during the air dry step.
Load RT-PCR reagent in the nanoport at the waste port.
Mix RNA with the RT-PCR reagent to prepare a 50 μl RT-PCR reaction.
Apply 35 V to heater 1 and keep the reagents in the RT channel for 30 min after the heater equilibrates at 50 °C.
Keep the reagents in the RT channel for 15 min after the heater equilibrates at 95 °C.
Apply 27 V to heater 1 and 50 V to heater 2, wait until both heaters reach 60 °C and 95 °C respectively.
Push the reagents into the PCR channel at a rate of 0.5 μl/min.
Collect the PCR products at the outlet using an appropriately sized pipettor when the sample reaches the end of the serpentine channel.
Load 1 μl of PCR products into the testing apparatus.
Follow the Agilent protocol for analysis.
Analyze and record the data.
